title: WP Admin Shell — admin.json (v3)
description: Declares a WP Admin Shell workspace — engine selection, branding, persistent chrome, the map of screens the workspace exposes, the engine-agnostic menu tree, command-palette bindings, REST preloads, and styles. v3 reshapes the document around user-task surfaces (`workspace` / `settings` / `screens` / `menu` / `commands`) instead of the v2 runtime-pipeline surfaces (`regions` / `routes` / `viewConfigs` / `bindings`). Cascade origins (core / engine / plugin / site / role / user) deep-merge per-field; arrays merge by `id`; `null` tombstones any property at any depth. Path collisions, permission-tier violations, and restrict-only enforcement are validated at resolve time, not by this schema. See `docs/v3/schema-sketch.md` for the full design rationale and `docs/wp-admin-shell-design-spec.md` for the runtime spec.

$schema.description: Reference to this schema document. Conventionally `https://schemas.wp.org/admin/v3.json`. Optional but strongly recommended — IDE tooling uses it for live validation. Relative paths are accepted (e.g., `../docs/schemas/admin-v3.json` for in-repo authoring) — `uri-reference` per RFC 3986, matching the block.json convention.

version.description: admin.json schema version this document targets. v3 is the current shape. The runtime accepts higher versions with a warning and best-effort load. v3 makes a clean break from v1/v2 — there is no automatic normalization from earlier shapes; authors migrating from v2 use a one-time migration helper documented in `docs/v3/schema-sketch.md`.

$wpds.description: Pinned WPDS slot matrix version, expressed as a WordPress release version (`6.9`, `7.0`, `7.1.2`). The resolver loads `wpds-defaults-{$wpds}.json` as the implicit `core` baseline so missing author values cannot break the runtime, and validates the `styles` tree against the WPDS slot list at this version. Bumping `$wpds` adopts new slots that may have appeared in later WordPress releases. CI parity tests guard against drift between this pin and the underlying WordPress version. Required because the WPDS surface is the shell's contract with apps and engines; an unpinned `styles` tree cannot be validated.

name.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this workspace on this install. Used in cascade origin storage, WP-CLI commands (`wp admin-shell activate <name>`), and the URL when a workspace-switcher exists. Must be unique within the install — registering a second workspace with the same name fails. Examples: `wp-admin-default`, `developer-admin`, `content-author`, `client-portal`, `acme-corp`.

title.description: Human-readable label for this workspace. Shown in the workspace-switcher UI (when enabled), admin-page metadata, plugin install screens. Translatable. Optional — absence falls back to `name`, but authors should provide it.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of what this workspace is for. Translatable.

user-switchable.description: When true, individual users may select this workspace as their personal default via the user prefs UI (overriding the site or role default). When false (default), only site admins and role configuration can select this workspace. Setting this true is forward-compatible — the cascade respects user-origin workspace selection regardless of UI availability.

workspace.description: Install metadata: engine, default landing screen, branding, system-chrome notices, and persistent widgets (toolbar / sidebar-footer / status-bar slots). Cascades deep-merge per-field; `workspace.widgets.<slot>` arrays merge by entry `id`. See schema-sketch.md §System chrome.

engine.description: Identifier of the engine that renders this workspace. References an `id` from a registered engine manifest. The engine determines spatial arrangement, region-template catalog, slot vocabulary, mode catalog, and which platform services are honored. Switching engines requires editing this field (and probably reworking advanced compositions in `regions` / `routes`) and reloads the workspace — engines are not live-switchable. Common values: `core:default` (flagship sidebar+content), `core:single-pane` (mobile-first drawer), `core:desktop` (windowed).

default-screen.description: Screen id (key into `screens`) where the workspace lands when no URL hash is present. Replaces v2's `default-route` — instead of a path, an id resolves to the screen's resolved `path`. On capability denial of the default screen, the workspace falls through to the first permitted screen with a `path`.

branding.description: Site-hub branding values. Engine-interpreted; `core:default` reads `logo` (URL or null) and `title` (string) for the sidebar header. Other engines may consume additional fields (e.g. `accent-color`) — the schema keeps this open. Cascade per-field.

notices.description: System-chrome notice slots. Workspace-scope (no path, no menu binding, never navigates). Engines render notices in their declared notice slots (`banner` at top-of-viewport, `snackbar` at bottom). Engines that omit notice slots ignore the block. Swap implementations by overriding `workspace.notices.banner.app` at any origin.

banner.description: Top-of-viewport notice host. Conventional pair with the engine's `banner` slot.

snackbar.description: Bottom-of-viewport ephemeral notification host. Conventional pair with the engine's `snackbar` slot.

widgets.description: Persistent workspace widgets — apps that mount across every screen, slotted into engine-declared workspace slots. Each property is a slot name (`toolbar`, `sidebar-footer`, `status-bar`, plus engine extensions); each value is an ordered array of widget entries. Cascade merges by entry `id` within each slot; new ids append. Engines without a given slot ignore the corresponding array. Plugins contribute via the `plugin` cascade origin; site admins hide individual entries via `hidden: true` or tombstone via `null`. See schema-sketch.md §Workspace widgets.

settings.description: Reusable definition registries that other parts of the workspace reference by id. Mirrors theme.json's `settings` pattern. v3 ships two registries: `dataViews` (entity-shape configuration for `@wordpress/dataviews`-driven apps) and `dataFields` (named field collections). Cascades deep-merge per-registry, per-entry. See schema-sketch.md §Settings.

dataViews.description: Global DataView registry keyed by `kind → name → variant`. Three axes: the kind matches `@wordpress/core-data` entity kinds (`postType`, `root`, `taxonomy`, etc.); the name is the specific entity (`post`, `page`, `user`, `comment`, `plugin`, `theme`); the variant id is author-defined kebab-case (`drafts`, `pending`, `trash`, `active`, etc.) with `_default` reserved for the implicit unqualified base. Each leaf is a complete `@wordpress/dataviews` configuration (`fields`, `defaultView`, `defaultLayouts`, `actions`, optional `fieldsRef`). Variants resolve independently per CIAB convention — there is no implicit `_default` merge; authors who want the v2 _default-merge convention declare `"extends": "_default"` on the variant entry. Filter `wp_admin_shell_data_view_config_{kind}_{name}` runs on the resolved doc per triple, plus `wp_admin_shell_data_view_config_{kind}_{name}_{variant}` whenever the variant ≠ `_default`. See `docs/plans/2026-05-20-dataview-registry-restoration.md` and spec §13 #7.

dataFields.description: Named field collections, keyed by collection id (slash-namespacing allowed, e.g. `core/post-fields`, `woocommerce/product-fields`). Each entry binds a set of field descriptors to an entity `(kind, name)` pair (or universal when `name` is null). DataViews reference a collection via `fieldsRef`; the runtime merges ref-wins-inline-overrides per-field. Renamed from v2 `fieldCollections`; moved under `settings.dataFields` for the registries grouping (paired with `settings.dataViews`). The per-descriptor word `field` stays — matches `@wordpress/dataviews` upstream. See schema-sketch.md §Fields and spec §13 #8.

screens.description: The map of every screen the workspace exposes, keyed by stable kebab-case id. Each entry defines what a screen IS (label, icon, apps, path, slot, mode, permissions, dataView, preload). Says nothing about where the screen appears in any menu — that's the `menu` block's job. Cascade deep-merges per-screen, per-field. `screens[id].apps[]` merges by entry `id`. `hidden: true` at any origin hides the screen from menus while still routable; tombstone via `null` to remove entirely. Implicit binding from menu items keyed by the same id flows label/icon/permissions automatically.

menu.description: Engine-agnostic information-architecture tree — a recursive map of nested items keyed by id. Containers are just items with children (no separate `groups` block). Item keys that match a screen id implicitly bind to that screen and inherit label/icon/permissions; keys that don't match a screen are standalone artifacts (group containers, external links via `href`, separators via `separator: true`). The active engine's `menu-renderer` decides how the tree displays (`core:default` → sidebar drilldown; `core:desktop` → dock; `core:single-pane` → drawer). Array-merge-by-id applies through every depth — `menu.content.items.posts.position: 5` at site origin reorders Posts under Content. See schema-sketch.md §Menu shape.

commands.description: First-class palette entries + keyboard shortcuts. Replaces v2's `bindings` array, broadened to include `navigate`-only entries (URL change without mounting a triggerable app) and surface labels for palette display. Each entry has a required `id`; cascade merges by `id` with later origins winning per-field. Tombstone via `null` on a matching `id` entry removes the command. See schema-sketch.md §Commands shape.

styles.description: WPDS-shaped style tree, unchanged from v2 — theme-developer surface intact. Authors override WPDS slot values (typically via DTCG token aliases into a sibling `tokens.json`) and shell-only chrome slots. Output is `--wpds-*` (full surface), `--wp-admin-shell--chrome--*` (chrome extensions), and a fixed compat bridge for legacy WordPress consumers. Per-region and per-app overrides live under `styles.regions[*]` and `styles.applications[*]`. See spec §9.

preload.description: Workspace-boot REST paths to preload server-side and inject as `wp.apiFetch.createPreloadingMiddleware` cache before the workspace bundle runs. Each entry is either a string path (defaults to GET) or a `[ path, method ]` tuple. Across cascade origins the resolved value is the additive concatenation of every origin's `preload[]` (no override semantics — site/role/user simply append). Duplicates by exact `path+method` are deduped before serialization. Per-screen preloads live in `screens[id].preload` — additive with this workspace-level list. See spec §13 #9.

regions.description: Escape hatch — direct region-tree authoring for engines that need it (windowed, MDI, multi-pane compositions). Optional in v3; the `screens` block synthesizes regions for the common case. When present, the resolver merges this tree on top of the screen-synthesized regions. See spec §5 for region semantics — same vocabulary as v2.

routes.description: Escape hatch — direct URL→app mapping for non-screen compositions. Optional in v3; screens with a `path` field synthesize routes for the common case. When present, cascade deep-merges by route key. See spec §6.2 — same vocabulary as v2.

namespacedId.description: A namespaced identifier referencing an app, engine, region template, or iframe escape-hatch target. Format: `core:{name}` (shell-shipped), `plugin:{slug}/{name}` (plugin-contributed), or `iframe:{url}` (wp-admin fallback — e.g. `iframe:options-permalink.php`). The iframe form is accepted on screen `app` fields per the wp-admin-default fixture; engine and template references reject it.

ariaRole.description: A WAI-ARIA 1.2 role name. See app manifest schema for the full description.

wpCapability.description: A WordPress capability slug (e.g. `read`, `edit_posts`, `manage_options`). Authoring tools that connect to a live install may pull `wp_roles()->get_capabilities()` for auto-completion.

wpRole.description: A WordPress role slug (e.g. `administrator`, `editor`, `author`, `contributor`, `subscriber`). The magic value `super-admin` triggers `is_super_admin($user_id)` — multisite-aware. The resolver treats unregistered role slugs as permanently-unsatisfiable requirements (fail-closed); typos can hide a screen but cannot accidentally expose one.

permissions.description: Access policy for a screen. Two array fields with OR semantics: a user passes if they hold ANY listed capability OR belong to ANY listed role. Between the two fields the result is OR-ed together. Absence of the block resolves to admin-only (`roles: [administrator, super-admin]`). The cascade applies trust-tier rules — `core`/`engine`/`plugin`/`site` origins may add or remove entries (full policy authority); `role` and `user` origins may only remove (shrink the OR-set), never grant themselves access. The app manifest's `capabilities[]` is an AND-floor untouchable by any workspace declaration: this block declares permitted access routes but cannot loosen the app's own requirements. See schema-sketch.md §Permissions.

capabilities.description: WordPress capability slugs the user must hold any one of to access this screen. Cascade merges by value (array-merge-by-identity). Tombstone individual values by setting the array to a tighter set at a higher origin (subject to trust-tier rules — role/user can only shrink).

roles.description: WordPress role slugs whose direct membership grants access to this screen. Special value `super-admin` triggers the multisite-aware `is_super_admin()` check. Cascade merges by value; trust-tier shrink-only at `role` and `user` origins.

screen.description: A workspace screen — a recognizable user-task surface. Defines what mounts, where the URL routes to, which engine chrome mode applies, and who can access it. v3 supports two app-declaration shapes: shorthand (single primary app via `app` + `config`) and long form (multi-app composition via `apps[]`). The resolver normalizes shorthand to `apps: [ { id: "main", app, config } ]` internally; cascade overrides always address the long-form `apps` array by entry `id`. Path uniqueness is runtime-validated (the resolver fails with a diagnostic if two screens claim the same resolved path); the schema only checks shape. See schema-sketch.md §Screen shape.

label.description: Human-readable screen label. Surfaces in menu items implicitly bound to this screen (unless overridden per-item), in the command palette, in browser tab titles. Translatable.

icon.description: Icon name resolved via the kernel icon registry (engine-populated). Surfaces in menu items implicitly bound to this screen (unless overridden per-item). Optional — screens without an icon render no icon in menu contexts.

description.description: Optional human-readable description. Surfaces as tooltip / drilldown subtitle in menu renderers that support it. Translatable.

path.description: URL path the screen routes from. Populates the `_self` URL slot by default. Parameter segments use `{name}` curly braces (e.g. `/posts/{id}/edit`); captured values flow into the screen's `config` via `{paramname}` substitution. Wildcard suffixes `/*` capture the remaining path. Path uniqueness across all screens is enforced at resolve time. Omit when the screen mounts in an alternate slot (e.g. `palette`).

slot.description: Workspace-scope URL slot this screen mounts in. Defaults to `_self` when `path` is set. Other kernel-reserved values: `palette` (command palette overlay). Engines may extend the slot vocabulary via `engine.json#slots` (e.g. `detail`, `inspector`). Slot vocabulary validated at resolve time against the active engine; unresolvable slots are rejected with a diagnostic. See schema-sketch.md §Slots.

app.description: Shorthand: app id to mount as this screen's primary content. Mutually exclusive with `apps[]` — use one or the other. Accepts `core:`, `plugin:`, and `iframe:` namespaces; `iframe:{wp-admin-script}` mounts a legacy wp-admin page (e.g. `iframe:options-permalink.php`). Resolver normalizes to `apps: [ { id: "main", app, config } ]` internally.

config.description: Shorthand: configuration object passed to the shorthand `app` at mount. Validated against the app manifest's `config-schema` before mount. URL parameter substitution applies: `{paramname}` strings in values resolve against captured path params (e.g. `{id}` in `/posts/{id}/edit` resolves to the captured id). Only meaningful with `app` shorthand; long-form `apps[]` carries per-entry config.

apps.description: Long form: multiple apps that mount when the screen activates. Each entry declares its own id (required), app, config, and optional screen-internal slot. The engine's layout algorithm arranges entries based on declared slots and available regions. Mutually exclusive with shorthand `app`/`config`. Cascade merges by entry `id`. Use for multi-pane / split-view compositions and dashboard-style screens with widgets. See schema-sketch.md §Multi-pane / split-view.

dataView.description: Inline overlay of the DataView configuration for this screen only. Same shape as a `settings.dataViews` registry entry; deep-merges on top of the resolved `(kind, name, variant)` triple looked up from `settings.dataViews`. Used to tweak one aspect of a registry triple per-screen (e.g. drop one field, override `defaultView.fields`) without forking the registry entry. Tombstone individual fields via `null`. The triple identity is resolved from `dataViewRef` first, then explicit `dataViewKind`/`dataViewName`/`dataViewVariant`, then inferred from the screen's primary `app` manifest's `dataView` block + `screen.config.{postType,taxonomy,variant}` (v2 back-compat path). Screens that don't address a registry triple may carry only an inline `dataView` doc (no overlay base) — escape hatch for one-off screens.

dataViewRef.description: Pointer into the `settings.dataViews` registry — `kind/name/variant`. Replaces the inferred-from-app-manifest lookup. When present, the resolved DataView doc is the registry triple plus any inline `dataView` overlay. Optional; absent triggers fallback inference from `dataViewKind`/`dataViewName`/`dataViewVariant`, then from the screen's primary `app` manifest's `dataView` block + `screen.config.{postType,taxonomy,variant}`. Mutually compatible with `dataView` overlay — overlay layers on top of the referenced triple via deep-merge with tombstones.

dataViewKind.description: Explicit DataView triple kind segment — alternative to `dataViewRef` when authors want to keep kind/name/variant in three separate fields (matches the field shape on the app manifest's `dataView` block). Matches `@wordpress/core-data` entity kinds (`postType`, `root`, `taxonomy`, etc.). Combined with `dataViewName` (required when this is set) and optional `dataViewVariant` (defaults to `_default`).

dataViewName.description: Explicit DataView triple name segment — alternative to `dataViewRef`. Names the entity (`post`, `page`, `user`, `comment`, etc.) under the kind declared in `dataViewKind`.

dataViewVariant.description: Explicit DataView triple variant segment — alternative to `dataViewRef`. Author-defined variant id (`drafts`, `pending`, `trash`, etc.) or `_default` for the unqualified base. Optional when `dataViewKind` + `dataViewName` are set; defaults to `_default`.

permissions.description: Access policy. Absent block resolves to admin-only. See `#/$defs/permissions` for OR-semantics and trust-tier cascade rules. The mounted app's `capabilities[]` AND-floor still applies regardless of what this block declares.

mode.description: Engine-defined chrome mode name. Common core values: `default` (full chrome), `focus` (strip nav + most toolbar — editor surfaces), `takeover` (all chrome hidden — customizer-style), `modal` (overlay on current screen). Engines declare their mode catalog in `engine.json#modes`; plugins extend via `wp_admin_shell_engine_modes_{engineId}` filter. Default when absent: `default`. See schema-sketch.md §Modes.

regions.description: Per-region override of the engine mode's region states. Escape hatch for cases the named mode doesn't cover (e.g. keep `preview` visible in `focus` mode). Keys are region ids declared by the engine; values are engine-defined state objects (typically `{ hidden, compact, minimal }`). Deep-merges with the engine's mode definition per-region, per-field. Tombstones via `null` to remove an override at a higher origin. See schema-sketch.md §Per-region override (escape hatch).

preload.description: REST paths to preload when this screen activates. Additive with the workspace-level `preload[]` block. Same shape as the workspace block: string path (GET shorthand) or `[ path, method ]` tuple. Useful for screen-specific hydration (e.g. `posts` preloading `/wp/v2/categories?context=view`).

hidden.description: When true, the screen is hidden from menu rendering but still routable by URL. Useful for palette-only screens, drill-target screens reached only via in-app links, modal-mounted screens. Different from tombstoning the screen entirely (`screens.<id>: null`) — `hidden: true` keeps the URL working.

allOf.description: Conditional rule: a screen cannot use both shorthand (`app`) and long form (`apps[]`). The two represent incompatible declarations — use one or the other. Resolver normalizes shorthand into long form before cascade.
Conditional rule: shorthand `config` only meaningful when shorthand `app` is also set. Long-form `apps[]` carries per-entry config.

appsEntry.description: A single entry in a screen's long-form `apps[]` array. Declares which app mounts, where inside the screen it lives (via screen-scope `slot`), what configuration it receives, and optional layout hints (`size`, `position`). The entry `id` is the cascade merge address — overrides at higher origins find the entry by id and deep-merge.

id.description: Stable entry id within the screen's `apps[]` array. Cascade addresses this entry by id; higher origins find a matching id and deep-merge per-field. New ids append. Convention: `main` for single-app shorthand normalization, descriptive kebab-case (`list`, `preview`, `recent-posts`) for multi-app screens.

app.description: App id to mount for this entry. Accepts `core:`, `plugin:`, and `iframe:` namespaces. The user must satisfy the app's `capabilities[]` AND-floor; otherwise the entry renders a 403 fallback (or is omitted from the screen's mount set, engine-defined).

config.description: Configuration passed to this entry's app at mount. Validated against the app manifest's `config-schema`. URL parameter substitution applies — `{paramname}` strings resolve against captured screen path params and URL query slots.

slot.description: Screen-scope slot name where this entry mounts inside the screen. Names an engine-declared slot (`detail`, `inspector`, `grid`) or an app-declared slot exposed by another entry in the same `apps[]` array (e.g. `core:dashboard-host` exposes a `grid` slot for widgets). Slot vocabulary validated at resolve time. Omitting `slot` mounts the entry in the screen's primary content region. See schema-sketch.md §Slots.

size.description: Optional layout hint for slot hosts that arrange entries spatially (e.g. dashboard widget grid). Engine / host honors hints as best-effort; layout algorithm has final say. Same shape as the v2 `dashboardWidgetSize` def.

position.description: Optional explicit placement for slot hosts that lay entries on a grid. `auto` (default) lets the layout algorithm place; `{row, col}` pins to a specific cell. Same shape as the v2 `dashboardWidgetPosition` def.

menuItem.description: A single menu tree node. Recursive — every item supports the same shape, and items with children declare them via the `items` map keyed by child id. Optional fields determine the item's role: an item with `items` is a container; an item with `href` is a link; an item with `separator: true` is a visual separator; an item whose key matches a screen id is implicitly bound to that screen (and inherits `label`/`icon`/`permissions` automatically). Tombstone an item at any depth by setting its value to `null`. See schema-sketch.md §Item shape.

label.description: Optional override of the bound screen's label. Required for items not bound to a screen (group containers, external links). When set on an item that is bound to a screen, renames the entry in the menu only — the screen itself is untouched.

icon.description: Optional override of the bound screen's icon. Required for items not bound to a screen. Children nested inside a parent menu item do NOT inherit the parent's icon — each item renders its own icon, and items without an icon render no icon. See schema-sketch.md §Drill-down icon inheritance.

position.description: Sort order among siblings at this depth. Lower numbers render earlier. Default = registration order. Cascade overrides reorder via `menu.<container>.items.<id>.position: <n>` at any origin.

items.description: Nested child items, keyed by id. Same shape recursively. Engines may impose a depth limit (default: 3) — items deeper than the limit are flattened or dropped per renderer policy.

href.description: External link target. Token interpolation supported (e.g. `{site_url}`, `{home_url}`). When present, the item renders as an anchor; `external: true` opens in a new tab.

external.description: When true with `href`, the link opens in a new browser tab (`target="_blank" rel="noopener"`).

separator.description: When true, the item renders as a visual separator. Other fields ignored — the renderer treats the entry as a divider only. Useful for grouping siblings into visual sections.

hidden.description: When true, the item is suppressed from rendering. The subtree is still addressable by cascade (so a higher origin can un-hide), unlike a `null` tombstone which removes the entry entirely.

command.description: A first-class command-palette entry, optionally with a keyboard shortcut. Replaces v2's `bindings` array, broadened. Each command must have an `id`; cascade addresses commands by id and deep-merges per-field. Tombstone via `null`. A command may declare `invoke` (mount a triggerable app), `navigate` (URL change without mounting), or both. `label` surfaces the command in the palette UI; absence means the command is keyboard-only. See schema-sketch.md §Commands shape.

id.description: Stable command id. Cascade merge address — higher origins find a matching id and deep-merge. Required. Tombstone the entry by setting its value to `null` at a higher origin.

shortcut.description: Keystroke specification, following @wordpress/keyboard-shortcuts syntax. `Mod+K` (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere), `Shift+Mod+P`, `Alt+ArrowDown`, `Mod+/`. Modifier names: `Mod`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Ctrl`. Sequence shortcuts (`g p`, `g m`) use a space separator. Optional — commands without a shortcut are palette-only entries.

invoke.description: App id to invoke. The app's manifest must declare `platform.triggerable: true`. When fired, the engine ensures the app's region is mounted (mounting if ephemeral) and applies the app's platform requests (focus trap, autofocus target). Mutually compatible with `navigate` — both may fire. Optional.

navigate.description: URL path the command navigates to. Pure shortcut to a screen — doesn't require an app to mount. Resolves against `screens[*].path`. Optional.

label.description: Human-readable command label for the palette UI. Surfaces the command even when keyboard-only. Translatable.

workspaceWidget.description: A persistent workspace widget — an app that mounts across every screen, slotted into an engine-declared workspace slot. Cascade merges by `id` within the slot array; new ids append. Tombstone via `null`. Slot-specific extra fields (e.g. `align: "end"` for toolbar, `size` for status-bar) ride along on the entry — schema is lenient (`additionalProperties: true`) because slot vocabulary is engine-defined. App-manifest `slotHints` provide defaults that the slot host honors when layout fields are absent. See schema-sketch.md §Workspace widgets.

id.description: Stable widget id within the slot array. Cascade merge address. Convention: descriptive kebab-case (`search`, `notifications-bell`, `help`).

app.description: App id to mount. Accepts `core:` and `plugin:` namespaces (iframe widgets are unusual but not prohibited). User must satisfy the app's `capabilities[]` AND-floor; otherwise the widget is omitted.

config.description: Optional configuration passed to the widget at mount. Validated against the app manifest's `config-schema`.

hidden.description: When true, the widget is suppressed from the slot. Use site/role/user origins to hide widgets the workspace ships with.

workspaceNotice.description: A workspace notice slot entry. Holds the app id that renders the notice surface (banner or snackbar). Swappable via cascade — `workspace.notices.banner.app: "plugin:my/sticky-banner"` at site origin replaces the default banner host.

app.description: App id to mount as the notice host. Conventional values: `core:notices-banner`, `core:notices-snackbar`. Apps that render notice queues consume the `@wordpress/notices` store internally.

settingsDataView.description: A DataView configuration document — describes how a `@wordpress/dataviews`-driven app should render a list/edit surface for a `(kind, name, variant)` triple (defined globally in `settings.dataViews.<kind>.<name>.<variant>`) or as a per-screen inline overlay (in `screens[id].dataView`). The shape is intentionally JSON-only — React render callbacks (column renderers, action modals) stay in the consuming app and are keyed off the declared `fields[].id` and `actions[].id`. Plugin engines shipping non-WPDS grids MAY ignore the block or interpret per their own conventions — the block is package-bound to `@wordpress/dataviews` when the active engine + apps consume it. See spec §13 #7 and `docs/plans/2026-05-20-dataview-registry-restoration.md`.

extends.description: Variant inheritance — names a sibling variant id under the same `(kind, name)` whose resolved doc this entry deep-merges on top of. No implicit `_default` merge (CIAB independent-resolution rule). Resolved recursively; max depth 10; cycles dev-warn and short-circuit. `_default` itself MUST NOT declare `extends`. Only meaningful on registry entries under `settings.dataViews[kind][name][variant]` or on app-manifest variant entries; ignored on per-screen inline overlays (`screens[id].dataView`).

fieldsRef.description: Reference to a `settings.dataFields` entry id. The referenced collection's `fields` array provides the base set; this entry's inline `fields` overrides per-field by `id`. Cascade pattern: ref wins, inline overrides per-field.

fields.description: Field descriptors for DataViews columns. Each entry declares an id (matches the entity record key), a type (text/datetime/number/select), a label, and optional filterability/searchability hints. Render callbacks are not declared here — the consuming app provides them keyed by id.

defaultView.description: Initial DataViews `view` object: `{ type, search, filters, page, perPage, sort, fields, titleField, layout }`. Used as the starting `view` state for the consuming app.

defaultLayouts.description: DataViews `defaultLayouts` prop. Keys are layout ids (`table`, `grid`, etc.); values are layout-specific config objects.

actions.description: Row-level + bulk action descriptors. Each entry declares an id (the consuming app maps to a callback), label, icon name, primacy/destructiveness flags, bulk support, and eligibility predicates expressed in declarative form. Custom modal render functions stay in the app.

_resolvedFieldsRef.description: Output-only debug stamp. The PHP resolver and JS hydration helper write this on the *resolved* DataView doc when a `fieldsRef` was resolved against a `settings.dataFields` entry; carries the source ref id so downstream debug snapshots can trace where columns came from. Authors do not declare it on inputs — Ajv accepts it on resolved-tree snapshots only.

dataViewField.description: A `@wordpress/dataviews` field descriptor in JSON form. Render callbacks (`render`, `Edit`) are out of scope — the consuming app provides them by mapping field id → renderer. Per-descriptor word `field` matches `@wordpress/dataviews` upstream; only the registry-level term `fields` was renamed to `dataFields`.

id.description: Field identifier. Matches the entity record key on the row data. Used by the consuming app to look up its render callback for this column.

type.description: DataViews field type. Drives the default editor/renderer when the consuming app doesn't ship a custom one.

enableHiding.description: When false, the column cannot be hidden from the table view. Default true.

enableGlobalSearch.description: When true, the column participates in DataViews' global search box. Default false.

enableSorting.description: When false, the column cannot be sorted. Default true for text/number/datetime.

elements.description: Enumerated values for select-type fields. Each entry is a `{ value, label }` pair.

filterBy.description: Filter configuration for this column. Omit to disable filtering.

dataViewAction.description: A `@wordpress/dataviews` row or bulk action descriptor in JSON form. The consuming app maps `id` to the actual callback (and optional `RenderModal`).

id.description: Action identifier. Stable across cascade overrides; consuming apps key their callback map off this value.

icon.description: Icon name resolved via the kernel icon registry (engine-populated). Optional.

isPrimary.description: When true, the action surfaces as a top-level affordance (row icon button, primary toolbar button) rather than buried in an overflow menu.

isDestructive.description: When true, the action triggers destructive UI affordances (red button, confirmation modal). Consuming apps render via the legacy `Button as DestructiveButton` fallback.

supportsBulk.description: When true, the action operates on a selection of multiple items, not just a single row.

eligibleWhen.description: Declarative eligibility predicate. Each property names a record field; the value is the required match (single value or array of valid values). Consuming app compiles to an `isEligible(item)` callback.

status.description: Item status(es) that make the action eligible. Examples: `"publish"`, `["publish", "future"]`.

dataFieldCollection.description: A named bundle of field descriptors bound to an entity `(kind, name)` pair. DataView entries reference a collection via `fieldsRef` to share field definitions across multiple variants. The collection is the *shape* of the entity's UI surface; DataView entries add *purpose* (which fields appear in this list, which actions fire). Renamed from v2 `fieldCollections`; moved under `settings.dataFields`. The per-descriptor word `field` matches `@wordpress/dataviews` upstream and is unchanged.

kind.description: Entity kind, matching `@wordpress/core-data` entity kinds (`postType`, `root`, `taxonomy`, etc.). Sanitized as `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`.

name.description: Entity name (`post`, `page`, `user`, `comment`). Null = universal across all names of the kind. Sanitized as `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`.

fields.description: Field descriptors that DataView entries may reference.

fieldsModule.description: Reserved. Native ESM script-module handle for client-side field extensions. Forward-compat declaration only — the shell runtime does not resolve or load this value. Real resolution wires up when the deferred native-script-modules + `.asset.php` build modernization arc lands. CIAB-compat field name.

styles.description: WPDS-shaped style tree. Top-level subtrees mirror the WPDS token matrix at the pinned `$wpds` version: `color`, `dimension`, `border`, `elevation`, `font`, `density`. Plus `chrome` (shell-only slots), `regions` (per-region overrides), `applications` (per-app overrides). Slot values may be DTCG token aliases (`{color.brand.500}`), literal CSS values (`#3858e9`, `16px`), or inline DTCG objects. The schema is intentionally loose at this level: WPDS slot validation is delegated to the runtime resolver against the pinned `$wpds` matrix, since the slot list grows with WordPress versions and embedding it here would freeze the schema to a specific version. Authors get IDE feedback on slot names from a runtime-generated companion schema rather than this static document.

theme.description: Seeds for `@wordpress/theme.ThemeProvider`. Primary customization path: pass seed values; the provider derives the full WPDS token matrix (color ramps, density-tuned dimensions). Maps 1:1 to ThemeProvider props. Allowed alongside `styles.regions[id].theme` and `styles.applications[id].theme` for nested provider overrides on a subtree.

primary.description: Primary/accent seed (default: `#3858e9`). Any valid CSS color. ThemeProvider derives `--wpds-color-{bg,fg,stroke}-interactive-brand-*` and the `--wp-admin-theme-color*` compat aliases from this. `null` tombstones a lower-origin override.

bg.description: Background seed (default: `#f8f8f8`). ThemeProvider derives the neutral surface ramp + fg-content-neutral from this and switches light/dark mode based on luminance. `null` tombstones a lower-origin override.

control.description: Cursor for non-link interactive controls (buttons, checkboxes, toggles). Default `pointer`.

density.description: Spacing scale. `compact` for data-dense surfaces; `comfortable` for focused panels. Equivalent to top-level `styles.density` (legacy).

color.description: Direct slot overrides (escape hatch). Authors emit specific `--wpds-color-*` slots when seeds can't express the desired override. Layers OVER ThemeProvider's seed-derived defaults via inner-scope CSS specificity.

chrome.description: Shell-only chrome extension slots — surfaces WPDS does not yet describe. Sub-namespaces include `sidebar`, `toolbar`, `siteHub`, `content`. Authors may add custom slugs; layout engines reading custom slugs declare them in their manifest's `requiredTokens` so the runtime validates at activation time.

regions.description: Per-region style overrides, keyed by region id. Same shape as the top-level `styles` tree. Overrides scope to `[data-region-id="..."]` selectors and win for that region's container and descendants.

applications.description: Per-app style overrides, keyed by app id. Same shape as the top-level `styles` tree. Overrides scope to `[data-app-id="..."]` selectors.

region.description: A region in the shell's region tree — escape hatch for compositions the `screens` block can't synthesize. Same vocabulary as v2: holds either a fixed app or accepts routed apps; never both. Can be instantiated from an engine-shipped template, declared from scratch, or appear as a nested child whose parent supplies template context. The schema does not enforce that every region has a resolvable `role` — that check is runtime-only, because the role may be inherited from the parent's template or from a template-shipped child of matching name, neither of which JSON Schema can reach across documents to validate.

template.description: Engine-shipped template id to instantiate. Inherits role, platform, and default-style from the template. Locally declared role/platform/style override the template; locally declared `regions` merge with the template's nested regions. Optional — when absent, the region is declared from scratch (and `role` becomes required).

role.description: ARIA role for the region. Required when no template is specified; optional override when a template is. See spec §5.1.

layout.description: CSS layout properties. Constrained to a layout-relevant subset (sizing, positioning, flexbox participation). Engines own layout context (`display`, grid templates) — the allowlist enforces this boundary. See spec §5.2.

platform.description: Platform service requests at the region level. Combined with the mounted app's manifest platform requests; the strictest combined request wins. See spec §5.3.

route-key.description: Names the URL slot whose value this region resolves to a route. `_self` reads the URL's primary path (typically only one region per shell uses `_self`). Any other value (e.g., `detail`, `inspector`) reads the same-named URL query parameter. See spec §5.4 and §6.4.

routing.description: URL participation declaration. A region with `route-key` is routable: the URL slot value at that key resolves to a route in the routes block, and the matching app mounts here. A region without `route-key` is non-routable (holds a fixed app or is purely chrome). See spec §5.4.

position.description: Arrangement hint for the engine. Used when declaring regions from scratch or overriding template arrangement. Engines decide how to honor the hint.

style.description: Style override for this region. CSS properties (background, border, color, padding, etc.) plus any `layout`-vocabulary properties. Token aliases (`{styles.color.bg.surface.neutral.strong}`, `{spacing.16}`) resolve at compile time.

capability.description: Install-level capability gate. Adds to the floor declared in the mounted app's `capabilities[]`. When the user lacks this capability, the entire region subtree (including any nested child regions) is skipped before mount.

app.description: App id to mount in this region for the life of the shell. Mutually exclusive with `routing.route-key`.

config.description: Configuration object passed to the mounted app at mount time. Only meaningful when `app` is set.

regions.description: Nested child regions, addressable as `{parent-id}/{child-id}` in the region tree. See spec §5.5.

allOf.description: Conditional rule: a region cannot have both a fixed `app` and `routing.route-key`. The two represent incompatible mount modes.
Conditional rule: `config` is only meaningful when `app` is also set.

regionLayout.description: CSS layout vocabulary allowlist. Engines own layout context (`display`, grid templates); authors declare only sizing, positioning, and flexbox participation. Properties accept literal CSS values or token aliases (resolved at compile time). Logical properties (`inline-size` / `block-size`) are preferred over physical (`width` / `height`) so layouts work in vertical writing modes.

regionPlatform.description: Platform service requests at the region level. Same vocabulary as the app manifest's `platform`; see app manifest schema for per-field description. Region-level requests combine with the mounted app's requests; strictest wins.

allOf.description: block-navigation-on-dirty requires dirty-state, same as in the app manifest.

route.description: A URL route entry — escape hatch for non-screen compositions. Maps a URL pattern to an app + config tuple. Same vocabulary as v2: there is no destination-region (`target`) field — the URL slot the pattern matched against determines which region mounts the route, via each region's `routing.route-key` declaration.

app.description: App id to mount when this route matches. The app must be discoverable via its manifest. The user must satisfy the app's `capabilities[]`; otherwise the route renders a 403 view.

config.description: Configuration passed to the mounted app. URL parameter substitution applies: `{paramname}` strings in values resolve against captured route params.

preloadEntry.description: A single REST preload declaration. String form is shorthand for a GET against the path. Tuple form `[ path, method ]` selects the verb explicitly. Paths are leading-slash REST routes (`/wp/v2/users/me`, `/wp/v2/types?context=view`); query-string `_fields` filters and other GET parameters are part of the path string. Methods mirror the verbs `rest_preload_api_request` understands.

prefixItems.description: REST path (leading slash; query string allowed).
HTTP verb. CIAB convention preloads only GET + OPTIONS — the WP REST controller dispatches OPTIONS for entity schema discovery.
